ceramic: {buyer} drinks from the {item} every morning and calls it 'artisan' to anyone who asks.
The {item} went to the office kitchen. It is the one nobody else is allowed to use.
{buyer} dropped the {item} once. It bounced. There is a photo.
wood: The {item} sits by {buyer}'s window. The cat has claimed it, obviously.
{buyer} shows the grain of the {item} to guests before they have taken their coats off.
The {item} was a wedding gift. The couple sends a card every year.
textile: The {item} lives on the good chair at {buyer}'s. Guests get the good chair.
{buyer} says the {item} is 'the only soft thing in the flat', and means it kindly.
A toddler named the {item}. The name stuck. The name is Pudding.
light: The {item} is on every evening at {buyer}'s. The neighbours set their clocks by it.
{buyer} reads under the {item}. Two chapters a night, three on Sundays.
The {item} made it into a magazine photo. Nobody told you. The magazine was small.
machine: The {item} rings on {buyer}'s desk and startles everyone, every time, forever.
{buyer} typed a letter to their mother on the {item}. She wrote back by hand.
The {item} keeps time in a hallway where nothing else works. People trust it.
fix: {buyer} put the {item} on a shelf at eye level. It is not for using. It is for looking at.
{buyer} says the {item} 'has character now', which is what you were going for.
The {item} went straight into a glass case. You did not expect that. Neither did it.
